text:
Alex K: Hey team — need a short-notice primary swap. I have a flight delay and won't be available 22:00–06:00 UTC tonight.

Alex K: Context: embed-service has shown a low-level 95p latency spike over the last ~20m (from ~120ms to ~340ms), error rate creeping +0.6% but no mass 5xx. A few customers reported slowness from EU. I'm asking for primary handoff so I can be offline and Morgan can own mitigation and paging during that window.

Alex K: Quick links/runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/embed-service-latency
Alex K: Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/embed-service/d/latency
Alex K: Quick health/check commands:```bash
# pod logs
kubectl logs -n inference -l app=embed-service --tail=200
# simple health
curl -sS http://embed-service.internal/api/health | jq .
```

Oncall Bot: IncidentBot: auto-detect — elevated latency on embed-service. Severity: P2 (monitoring). No pager triggered. Linked incident INC-18433.

Morgan L: I can take primary for 22:00–06:00 UTC. A couple Qs before I flip: is traffic skewed to a particular region or client? Any recent deploys? I'll shadow you for ~10–15m prior to go-time.

Alex K: No deploys in last 3 hours. Traffic spike is EU-heavy — looks like a client stuck in old retry-loop increased token fan-out. See the per-region panel. No obvious memory/ooms.

Alex K: Numbers: 95p latency 340ms, median ~90ms, error-rate +0.6% over baseline (mostly timeouts/retries), request volume +1.7x from eu-west-1 for last 25m.

Jamie R: Quick idea — check prefix cache hit-rate and KV eviction. If cache fill dropped that could explain tail latency. From runbook section "cache-warm":```bash
# check kv metrics
curl -sS http://embed-service.internal/metrics | grep prefix_cache_hit_rate
```
Jamie R: If hit-rate < 85% try the warming job (runbook has the command), and consider routing 20% to fallback model variant (embed-small-quant) if tail persists.

Morgan L: Good call. I'll check cache metrics and kick the warming job if needed. Can someone add Esther as secondary for the window? Also I'll update PD ownership and post a check-in after warm-up.

Esther P: Ack — I'll be secondary for 22:00–06:00 UTC and will monitor support queue. Will watch for customer DMs and escalate if pages fire.

Alex K: Hand-off checklist (short):
• Update PagerDuty ownership: assign "embed-service" primary to Morgan L (PD assignment UI or `pd assign` if you have CLI).
• Post brief in #incidents that Morgan is primary for window + link to INC-18433.
• Run through cache/warm steps and confirm canary traffic is OK.
• Leave INC-18433 note with what you changed.

Alex K: PD CLI example (if you use it):```bash
pd-incident assign INC-18433 --assignee "Morgan L" --note "primary swap 22:00-06:00 UTC (Alex out)"
```

Oncall Bot: ScheduleUpdate: Morgan L set as primary 22:00–06:00 UTC, Esther P set as secondary.

PagerDuty Bot: Ownership changed for service=embed-service, incident=INC-18433, assignee=Morgan L.

Morgan L: Taking it — will do a 15m shadow now (watching caches + rw-edges), then flip routing and confirm via a quick post here. I'll start with: check cache hit-rate + tail latency panel, warm caches, run small canary (5% traffic) to embed-small-quant if tail persists.

Morgan L: Quick check-in in ~12m. Alex — leaving you reachable via DMs if anything urgent comes up. :thumbsup:

Alex K: Thanks Morgan, appreciate it. Leaving a note in INC-18433 as I step out.

Esther P: I'll keep the support queue hot and watch for customer-impact flags. Ping me if you open an escalated page.

Morgan L: Confirmed — I updated the on-call schedule and PD ownership, warming caches now. Will report back with results or flip to fallback if no improvement in 20m.
